summary: Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Notre Dame, University of New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, and held posts at Northwestern University (~1993–1995) and the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon was an archaeologist who studied at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College, Oxford. She held posts at the University of London (~1937–1962), the UCL Institute of Archaeology (1948–1962), and St Hugh's College, Oxford (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She held academic posts at DePauw University (~1984–1986), the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1986–1987), Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).

Kathleen McDonald is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Attested in 2010, she studied under traditional teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, Yeshe Thubten, Lama Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Ngawang Dhargyey, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Ribur Rinpoche.
Kathrin Holz works in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Würzburg under Ingo Strauch and held a research affiliation at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Kathryn H. Selig Brown is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Michigan by 2000, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Walter M. Spink.

Katia Buffetrille is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Paris Nanterre University under Alexander W. Macdonald, later holding posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002) and the Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale.

Katragadda Paddayya is an archaeologist and Indologist. After completing his doctorate at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1963–1968), he held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as Professor (~1970) and Professor of Geo-archaeology (attested 2026).

Katrin Querl is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Vienna. As of 2026, she is attested as a Wissenschaftliche Mitarbeiterin and lecturer for Tibetan at the University of Hamburg.

Katsuhiko Kamimura was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Madras under Minoru Hara and V. Raghavan. His career included posts at the University of Tokyo and Kokugakuin University, among other institutions.
Katsuhiro Yoshizawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 2006).

Katsuji Fujioka was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and Leipzig University (1901–1905). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Tokyo from 1910 to 1933.
Katsumi Kuroita was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896) and later held a post there from approximately 1908 to 1935.

Katsumi Mimaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Kyoto University, INALCO, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and the University of Paris under Gadjin M. Nagao, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Hisashi Sato, later serving as professor at Kyoto University (1996–2010).

Katsumi Okimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Hanazono University (~1988–2014) and as director of the International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism (attested 2009).

Katsumi Tanabe is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1964–1970) and held posts at Kanazawa University (~1990–1997) and Chuo University (~1997–2011).

Katsutoshi Ono was an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and sinologist. He studied at Kyoto University, later working at Kyoto University (1933–1943), the Eastern Cultural Institute's Beijing Branch (~1938–1945), Nara National Museum (1949–1967), and Ryukoku University (~1970–1980).

Kausthub Desikachar works in philosophy and Indology. He founded Viniyoga Singapore and the Krishnamacharya Healing and Yoga Foundation, served as Executive Trustee at Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram until 2012, and is Chief Executive at the Krishnamacharya Healing and Yoga Foundation.

Kavita Singh was an art historian and Indologist who studied at Lady Shri Ram College, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, Panjab University, and University of the Punjab. She held posts at Marg Publications, San Diego Museum of Art, and Jawaharlal Nehru University.

Kazi Dawa Samdup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Bhutia Boarding School under Ugyen Gyatso and Tshampa Norbu, he later served as headmaster there (~1906–1919) and as a lecturer at the University of Calcutta in 1920.
